BillHeading.Sponsors: Representatives Shea, McCaslin, Scott, Taylor, Holy, G. Hunt, and Condotta
BillHeading.BriefDescription: Repealing unnecessary provisions concerning the Washington State Bar Association.

BillSectionHeader.P: The legislature finds that the Washington State Bar Association was initially established by the legislature as a state agency. Since that time the State Supreme Court has taken over as the entity regulating members of the state bar, and has opined that, "the ultimate power to regulate court-related functions, including the administration of the Bar Association, belongs exclusively to this court." WSBA v. State of Washington, 125 Wn.2d 901 (1995). Therefore, the legislature intends to repeal statutes establishing the bar association and regulation of members of the bar.
The following acts or parts of acts are each repealed:

(2) RCW 2.48.020 (First members) and 1933 c 94 s 3;
(3) RCW 2.48.021 (New members) and 1933 c 94 s 4;

(13) RCW 2.48.110 (Admission of veterans—Fees of veterans) and 1945 c 181 s 5;

BillSectionHeader.P: RCW 2.48.180, 2.48.190, and 2.48.200 are each recodified as sections in chapter 2.44 RCW.
